extracted.intended_audience: general readers, writers and critics interested in the Literary Review magazine and its Bad Sex in Fiction Award
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and editorial stance surrounding the Literary Review's Bad Sex in Fiction Award and the magazine's remit — i.e., how the award selects 'bad' sex scenes and what the magazine publishes. Useful for writers, critics, and editors thinking about sexual description in literary fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worst description of a sex scene
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bad Sex in Fiction Award is "presented the annual Bad Sex in Fiction Award to the author it deems to have produced the worst description of a sex scene in a novel."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Established by Rhoda Koenig and Auberon Waugh; symbolically presented as a trophy. The award's operational selection is centered on identifying the single 'worst' sexual description in a given year among novels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim — discourage crude, tasteless, redundant sexual description
rubrics_metrics.description: The stated aim: "to draw attention to the crude, tasteless, often perfunctory use of redundant passages of sexual description in the modern novel, and to discourage it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on passages judged crude/tasteless/perfunctory or redundant. Implies a normative standard for writers: avoid unnecessary or lazy sexual description that does not serve the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude pornography/erotica; target mainstream literary fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The award "deliberately avoids shortlisting actual pornography or erotica and instead targets authors who are trying to be honest about desire and sex, however distasteful the results may be."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection policy is aimed at mainstream/literary novels rather than explicit pornographic or erotic works; the target is unsuccessful attempts at honest sexual depiction rather than works whose primary intent is eroticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical/critical concern — avoid public shaming
rubrics_metrics.description: The enduring relevance of this rationale has been questioned, based on concerns about censorious public shaming (including online) of authors of serious literary fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics argue the award can encourage misreading of fiction, conflating authors with characters and publicly shaming writers; evaluators should consider the ethical implications of public ridicule and the context of the passage within the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial remit — breadth of published material
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary Review "reviews a wide range of published books, including fiction, history, politics, biography and travel, and additionally prints new fiction."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an editorial guideline, the magazine's remit includes reviews across multiple genres and the publication of original fiction; submissions and evaluations should align with this broad scope.
